illegal_break.trigger: 4.3(d): nothing pocketed and fewer than four distinct object balls driven to rails (WPA 4.3(d) illegal break)

break_foul.trigger: 4.3(f)(g)(h): a break foul other than the 8-on-break cases

stalemate.trigger: 4.11 with WPA 1.13's by-agreement path: both players agree the rack is a stalemate

entries.name: Clean break - a ball pocketed, breaker continues, table stays open

target_facts.summary: A ball pocketed with no foul is a legal break (4.3(c)); the breaker continues and the table stays open.

entries.note: WPA 4.3(c): a ball pocketed on the break with no foul - the breaker continues and the table stays open (no group is assigned on the break; 4.4). The four-distinct-object-balls requirement of 4.3(d) applies only when nothing is pocketed.

entries.name: Legal break - exactly four distinct object balls to rails, nothing pocketed

target_facts.summary: Nothing pocketed but exactly four distinct object balls reach rails - clean legal break; the turn passes.

adjudication.legality: legal_break_clean (4.3(d)); four distinct object balls to rails

entries.note: WPA 4.3(d) boundary: four distinct object balls is exactly sufficient. The predicate is per ball (2.7), so ball 5's single rail contact counts once; ball 9's counts once. Nothing pocketed, no foul, turn passes.

entries.name: Legal break by pocket with only three object balls to rails

target_facts.summary: A ball pocketed with only three object balls to rails is still a legal break (precedence 2): the count condition is not evaluated once a ball is pocketed.

adjudication.legality: legal_break_by_pocket (4.3(c)); precedence 2 over the rail count

entries.note: WPA 4.3(c) read with 4.3(d): the four-object-balls-to-rails requirement is conditioned on nothing being pocketed, so a pocket makes the break legal however few balls reached rails. Classification precedence: 8-on-break > pocketed > rail count.

entries.name: Total miss of the rack - illegal break, not a foul

target_facts.summary: The cue ball never touches the rack, nothing is pocketed and no ball reaches a rail: illegal break under 4.3(d) and no foul (3.2/3.3 are not evaluated on the break).

options.description: Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again
Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again

entries.note: WPA 4.3(b) removes any first-contact requirement on the break and 4.3(d) supplies the break's own legality rule, so 3.2/3.3 are not evaluated on this shot and the record carries no foul: the classification is the illegal break alone. The three options offered to the incoming player are 4.3(d)'s, none of which is ball-in-hand.

entries.name: Soft break - three object balls to rails, nothing pocketed

target_facts.summary: Three object balls to rails with nothing pocketed: illegal break; the cue ball finishing above the head string changes nothing.

adjudication.legality: illegal_break_clean (4.3(d)); three distinct object balls to rails

options.description: Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again
Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again

entries.note: WPA 4.3(d): a soft break is illegal only when it also fails the pocket-or-four-balls test; three distinct object balls to rails fails it. Where the cue ball rests is irrelevant to the classification.

entries.name: Illegal break with a scratch - the illegal-break tree governs

target_facts.summary: Illegal break that is also a foul (scratch): the illegal-break tree governs and offers 4.3(d)'s three options; no ball-in-hand anywhere.

adjudication.legality: illegal_break_with_foul (4.3(d) + 3.1); illegal-break tree precedence per CSI 2-3-3

options.description: Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again
Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again

entries.note: Deviation line: WPA is silent on a break that is both illegal (4.3(d)) and a foul; CSI 2-3-3 makes the illegal break take precedence, so the illegal-break tree governs and the scratch adds no ball-in-hand. 4.3(d)'s options grant no ball-in-hand anywhere, so a scratch's anywhere remedy (4.9) is subsumed. The cue-ball-aware option behaviour is in the option-1 follow-up (rb-26).

entries.name: Illegal break with an object ball driven off the table

target_facts.summary: Illegal break plus an object ball off the table: the illegal-break tree still governs; the off-table ball stays off (only the 8 is ever spotted).

adjudication.legality: illegal_break_with_foul (4.3(d) + 3.5); illegal-break tree precedence per CSI 2-3-3

options.description: Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again
Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again

entries.note: Deviation line: CSI 2-3-3 precedence (WPA silent). Ball 15 stays out of play; had the off-table ball been the 8, precedence 1 would instead route the shot to the 8-on-break handling with the 8 spotted (4.7) - the same illegal-break tree would not govern. Spotted is empty here because the off-table ball is not the 8.

entries.name: Frozen-to-rail edge - a nudge that stays does not count

target_facts.summary: Two object balls were frozen to rails at shot start: ball 5 was nudged but stayed frozen and does not count, ball 15 left and returned and does count - three distinct object balls, so the break is illegal.

options.description: Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again
Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again

entries.note: WPA 2.7: a ball touching a rail at the start of the shot is not driven to that rail unless it leaves and returns. Ball 5's rail contact is a nudge that never separated it (a contact event, but not a counted ball); ball 15 separated and came back (counted). Pre-state note: no fresh rack can contain a rail-frozen object ball, so this entry declares a synthetic pre-state (`target_facts.expected.pre_state`) isolating 2.7 inside 4.3(d)'s count; the predicate is equally live on any later shot.

entries.name: Same ball to two rails plus two others - three distinct, illegal

target_facts.summary: Ball 7 reaches two rails and balls 2 and 15 reach one each: four rail contacts but only three distinct object balls - illegal break.

adjudication.legality: illegal_break_clean (4.3(d)); per-ball predicate, contacts are not counted

options.description: Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again
Re-rack and allow the offending player to break again

entries.note: WPA 2.7 read with 4.3(d): the requirement is four distinct object balls driven to one or more rails - a ball can hit several rails and is still one ball. Contact count 4, distinct balls 3, illegal.

entries.name: One ball to two rails plus three others - four distinct, legal

target_facts.summary: Ball 13 reaches two rails and balls 1, 9 and 14 one each: five contacts, four distinct object balls - legal break.

adjudication.legality: legal_break_clean (4.3(d)); four distinct object balls to rails

entries.note: The boundary of rb-09: the same double-rail ball plus three others gives four distinct object balls. Distinctness, not contact count, decides 4.3(d).

entries.name: 8 pocketed on a legal break, fewer than four to rails

target_facts.summary: The 8 is pocketed on a break with no foul and fewer than four object balls to rails: the 8-on-break tree outranks the rail count (precedence 1); the breaker chooses between spotting the 8 and re-breaking.

options.description: Spot the 8-ball and accept the balls in position
Spot the 8-ball and accept the balls in position

entries.note: WPA 4.3(e): pocketing the 8 on a legal break is neither a foul nor a win; the breaker may spot the 8 and accept the balls in position, or re-break. Classification precedence 1: the 8-on-break trees govern regardless of the rail count.

entries.name: 8 pocketed on a foul break - opponent's two options

target_facts.summary: The 8 is pocketed on a break that also fouls (scratch): the 8-on-break foul tree governs (precedence 1); the opponent may spot the 8 and shoot with cue ball in hand above the head string, or re-break. Option 1 spots the 8.

options.description: Spot the 8-ball and shoot with cue ball in hand above the head string
Spot the 8-ball and shoot with cue ball in hand above the head string

entries.note: WPA 4.3(f): opponent's options are (1) re-spot the 8 and shoot with cue ball in hand above the head string, or (2) re-break. Precedence 1 again, and the cue-ball domain is above_the_head_string - never anywhere.

entries.name: 8 driven off the table on the break - spotted, break-foul tree

target_facts.summary: The 8 is driven off the table on the break: the 8-on-break handling governs (precedence 1, rail count not consulted), the 8 is spotted, and - because a ball off the table is itself a foul (3.5) - the opponent chooses between spotting the 8 with cue ball in hand above the head string and re-breaking.

options.description: Spot the 8-ball and shoot with cue ball in hand above the head string
Spot the 8-ball and shoot with cue ball in hand above the head string

entries.note: WPA 4.7 read with 4.3(f): the 8 pocketed or driven off the table on the break is spotted - or the rack is re-formed - and the 8-on-break trees govern (precedence 1, so the rail count is not consulted even though four distinct object balls reached rails here). A ball driven off the table is itself a foul (3.5), so the opponent chooses: spot the 8 and shoot with cue ball in hand above the head string, or re-break. 4.3(g)'s remedy is for object balls off the table, never the 8. With no foul on the same shot the same 8-on-break handling gives the breaker the choice instead (4.3(e); see rb-11/rb-31).

entries.name: Foul on an otherwise legal break - cue-ball in hand above the head string

target_facts.summary: Four distinct object balls to rails makes the break legal, but the scratch is a break foul: the incoming player may accept the table in position or take cue ball in hand above the head string - never anywhere.

adjudication.legality: break_foul (4.3(h)); the break itself is legal by 4.3(d)

options.description: Take cue ball in hand above the head string
Take cue ball in hand above the head string

entries.note: The break legality test and the foul are independent: 4.3(d)'s count is satisfied, yet the foul routes to 4.3(h). After a break foul the incoming player's cue-ball-in-hand domain is above the head string, never anywhere (contrast 4.9's anywhere after a standard foul during play).

entries.name: Object ball off the table on a legal break

target_facts.summary: An object ball is driven off the table on an otherwise legal break: break foul under 4.3(g); the ball stays off (only the 8 is ever spotted) and the break-foul tree is offered.

adjudication.legality: break_foul (4.3(g)); object ball stays off per 4.7

options.description: Take cue ball in hand above the head string
Take cue ball in hand above the head string

entries.note: WPA 4.3(g) read with 4.7: only the 8 is ever spotted, and only from the break; ball 15 stays out of play. No spotting here because the off-table ball is not the 8.

entries.name: Classification tie inside one simultaneity group

target_facts.summary: Two first contacts land inside one simultaneity group (the cue ball on ball 2 and the 8); the group is resolved in favour of legality and its id is carried into the adjudication.

adjudication.legality: legal_break_by_pocket (4.3(c)); simultaneity group 0 resolved legality-favourably (3.2, Reg 25)

entries.note: The simulation reports a deterministic order plus simultaneity groups for contacts it cannot order within epsilon; the rules layer's tie-break resolves in favour of legality (3.2's legal-ball-assumed-first, Reg 25's default-to-legal) and the group id travels with the adjudication - never the simulator's internal order. On the break 4.3(b) removes any first-contact requirement, so the tie cannot change the verdict; this row pins the group-carrying machinery that is live off the break.

target_facts.summary: A ball pocketed and four distinct object balls to rails: legal on both conditions; the breaker continues on an open table.

Pre-state note: no fresh rack can contain a rail-frozen object ball, so the frozen status is declared as a synthetic pre-state in `target_facts.expected.pre_state`; the row isolates the predicate that 4.3(d)'s count consumes.

entries.name: Stalemate declared by mutual agreement - re-rack applied

target_facts.summary: Stalemate by mutual agreement: the rack is re-racked from the same seed with the original breaker breaking again; all 15 object balls are back on the table and no shot was adjudicated.

options.description: Re-rack and the original breaker breaks again (mutual agreement)

entries.note: Input event, not a shot: the mutual agreement is a declared input, so the entry carries no `facts` stream (the schema's fact vocabulary is simulation-only: ball_ball/rail/pocket/off_table). `rest` records the mid-rack table the agreement abandoned. Rule pair: WPA 1.13's by-agreement path (both players accept the stalemate without the referee's three-turn procedure) + 4.11's remedy (the original breaker of the rack breaks again). Deviation line: 1.13's referee-mediated no-progress detection is dropped - no referee - so mutual agreement is the only stalemate path.

entries.name: Stalemate re-rack restores a ball pocketed earlier in the rack

target_facts.summary: A ball had been pocketed earlier in the abandoned rack; the stalemate re-rack puts all 15 object balls back on the table - contrast the break trees, where pocketed balls stay down.

expected.contrast: break-tree accept options leave pocketed balls down

options.description: Re-rack and the original breaker breaks again (mutual agreement)

entries.note: Input event, not a shot. Ball 6 had been pocketed during the abandoned rack (hence absent from `rest`); the re-rack restores the full 15-ball snapshot, so it is back on the table. This is the contrast with the break trees' accept-in-position, which never returns a pocketed ball (4.7: no object ball is ever spotted except the 8, and only from the break).

entries.name: Stalemate re-rack of a later rack of the match

target_facts.summary: The stalemated rack is rack 2 of the match, so the restored arrangement is that rack's snapshot - fixture 2 - and not the first rack's arrangement.

expected.note: seed = splitmix64 fold of (match_seed, rack_index); the first rack's fixture is not reused

options.description: Re-rack and the original breaker breaks again (mutual agreement)

entries.note: Input event, not a shot. Per-rack seed derivation lives in the match layer: rack i's seed is a splitmix64 fold of (match_seed, rack_index) and re-racks reuse that rack's seed, so a stalemate on rack 2 restores fixture 2's positions even though fixture 0 exists. Alternating breaks (1.3) make the original breaker of rack 2 the same player who broke rack 0 in a two-player match.

entries.name: Stalemate re-rack vs illegal-break re-rack for the same seed

target_facts.summary: The same seed re-racked from a stalemate and from the illegal-break tree restores the identical arrangement; only the breaker flag differs (option 2 advances the rotation to the opponent, option 3 keeps the offender, stalemate keeps the original breaker).

options.description: Re-rack and the original breaker breaks again (mutual agreement)

Cross-reference: this entry mirrors the illegal-break follow-ups rb-18 (option 2, re-rack and break) and rb-19 (option 3, re-rack and the offender breaks again) - all three restore fixture 0's arrangement with the seed unchanged and the shot counter reset; the breaker flag is the only difference, which is exactly what the three re-rack options mean. Rule pair for this entry: WPA 1.13/4.11.

entries.name: Stalemate proposed and agreed - the pending-choice entrance

target_facts.summary: The mutual agreement raises the stalemate offer: the rack is abandoned and the single remedy - re-rack and the original breaker breaks again - is the pending choice that sb-01..sb-04 apply.

adjudication.legality: stalemate_declaration; offer raised (WPA 1.13 by-agreement path, 4.11 remedy)

options.description: Re-rack and the original breaker breaks again (mutual agreement)
Re-rack and the original breaker breaks again (mutual agreement)

entries.note: Input event, not a shot: the agreement is a declared input, so the entry carries no `facts` stream (the schema's fact vocabulary is simulation-only: ball_ball/rail/pocket/off_table). This is the entrance the stalemate family hangs off: the tree has exactly one option and the agreement fixes it, so `chosen_option` is recorded here while `state` remains the pending choice; sb-01..sb-04 apply it (sb-01 plain, sb-02 with a pocketed ball restored, sb-03 on a later rack, sb-04 cross-checked against the illegal-break re-racks). Rule pair: WPA 1.13 by-agreement path + 4.11 remedy.
